Definition: probably strengthened from φθίω (to pine or waste); properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave):--corrupt (self), defile, destroy.
BiblicalUsage: Phtheiro means to spoil, to ruin something from the inside out. Paul warns that evil communications corrupt good manners in 1 Corinthians 15:33, and fears the serpent will corrupt the Corinthians' minds from the simplicity in Christ in 2 Corinthians 11:3. It is the old man growing corrupt in Ephesians 4:22, and the whore who corrupted the earth in Revelation 19:2.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe corruption is never neutral — it spreads from one bad companion, one lie, one lust, until the whole thing is ruined. That is why I hold that God judges the corrupter and not only the corrupted, as 1 Corinthians 3:17 says of the man who defiles His temple.
